label: prf:q-casimir-unique
title: Proof of uniqueness of the $q$-Casimir element
html:
The centre Z(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))) is a polynomial ring in C_q over the ground ring (Joseph--Letzter, Kassel VI.4.9). Any central element therefore belongs to R[C_q]; in particular, the identity plus a linear term a + b C_q is the only linear-in-C_q central element.

Fixing the eigenvalue on V_j to be [j]_q[j+1]_q (for all j) pins down the coefficient b = 1 and the constant a such that the eigenvalue vanishes on the trivial representation (V_0: [0]_q[1]_q = 0, so a = 0). Hence C_q is unique. Other normalisations (e.g. the non-symmetric q-Casimir C'_q = C_q + \text{const}) differ by a scalar shift, which is absorbed into the ground ring.
